description: A theme's master: its settings and the artwork every slide shows.

markdownpoint.description: The format version. It is a major and a minor number in quotes: "1.0".

id.description: The theme's identity, a lowercase UUID. It stays the same when the theme is renamed, added under another key, or carried in a theme package. It tells apart two themes with the same key.

name.description: The theme's name: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. The default is the theme's key with spaces for its hyphens and a capital first letter.

category.description: The category the theme is listed under: essentials, business, education, community, or personal. With any other word, it is listed under Other.

size.description: The slide size. The default is 1920 × 1080.

unit-scale.description: The length of one canvas unit in meters. At 0.001, a canvas unit is a millimeter, and one meter of a model's GLB spans 1,000 canvas units. The default is 0.001.

fonts.description: The font family for each font role.

display.description: The family for headings and large type.

font-files.description: The theme's embedded fonts by family name. Each is a list of .eot files for a family a font role uses. There is one per face.

brand.description: The brand's named colors. Schemes use them.

colors.description: The brand's hex colors by name.

schemes.description: The theme's color schemes by name. Every theme has light and dark.

font-family.description: The font role the text uses. The theme sets a font family for each role.

font-weight.description: The font weight: 300 light, 400 regular, 500 medium, 600 semibold, 700 bold, or 900 black.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

line-height.description: The distance between lines in multiples of the font size.

case.description: The letter case the text is shown in. The text itself stays as typed. With `title`, the first letter of each word is a capital.

padding-top.description: The space between the text box's top and its first line.

padding-bottom.description: The space between the text box's last line and its bottom.

list-indent.description: How far each list level indents.

bullet-styles.description: The bullet at each list level in order from the first. The last one is used at every deeper level.

marks.description: How bold, italic, highlighted, struck-through, and code text look in this style.

font-family.description: The font role the text uses. The theme sets a font family for each role.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

case.description: The letter case the text is shown in. The text itself stays as typed. With `title`, the first letter of each word is a capital.

bold.description: How bold text looks. Its weight is 700, or the text's weight if that is heavier. It replaces any weight inside the bold. So bold has no `font-weight`. Without it, bold uses the text's font.

highlight.description: How highlighted text looks. It is colored and has no background. By default, it is the accent color at weight 600 and never lighter than the text around it.

code.description: How code looks. By default, it is the mono font at 0.92 times the text's size.

text-styles.description: The theme's text styles by name. No name is built in.

items.description: One ruler guide. It has `x` or `y`, not both.

id.description: The guide's id, unique among the master's guides.

x.description: How far a vertical guide is from the slide's left edge.

y.description: How far a horizontal guide is from the slide's top edge.

name.description: The guide's name: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

locked.description: Whether the guide is locked against dragging.

grid.description: The layout grid: columns and a baseline grid.

gutter.description: The space between columns. The default is 0.

margin.description: The margin on the left and on the right. The default is 0.

start.description: How far the first baseline is from the slide's top.

default-step-duration.description: The default length of a newly added step. Its fades and moves last this long, and its `min-duration` is this length. A by-paragraph delivery starts with this length. The default is 0.5.

layout-order.description: The order of the layouts by key. Each is listed once. Unlisted layouts follow in key order.

frame.description: An object's position and size in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's, an audio object's, and a group's frame has only x and y: their contents, an icon, or members give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom. A group has a frame only with `auto-layout`. Its frame is the position of its members' box. Its `reference-point` says which point of the box that is: the top left in the group's rotation, or the middle or end along the layout's direction.

x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. For a group, it is the point `reference-point` names.

y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows and it has no `anchor-point`, it turns and scales about a point on its top edge. For a group, it is the point `reference-point` names.

text-path.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame

anyOf.description: A text's drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. Its lengths are in ems of the text's font size. First, the text's letters and outline grow solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far the shadow reaches beyond the text's letters and outline. Photoshop's Size works the same way.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls: {x, y} across and down in the text's own axes. It turns and scales with the text and its groups.

color.description: Its color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

anyOf.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

A theme object's file for each color scheme. A dark scheme can then use a file of its own. An image, video, audio, or model object can have a file map in place of a single file. Every file in the map is the same type. A placeholder has one file, not a map.

light.description: The file for the light scheme, and for other light schemes without their own.

dark.description: The file for the dark scheme, and for other dark schemes without their own.

mask.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame

image-style.description: nonempty text without NUL characters, or "none"

restyle.description: A style applied over an image or a background's image. It has every key of a library style except `reference-image-prompt`.

name.description: The style's name: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

prompt.description: How the style changes an image: an edit prompt. It isn't blank.

transparent-background.description: Whether images in the style have transparent backgrounds.

anyOf.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

A theme object's file for each color scheme. A dark scheme can then use a file of its own. An image, video, audio, or model object can have a file map in place of a single file. Every file in the map is the same type. A placeholder has one file, not a map.

light.description: The file for the light scheme, and for other light schemes without their own.

dark.description: The file for the dark scheme, and for other dark schemes without their own.

additionalProperties.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

poster.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

tail.description: The tip of a speech bubble's tail.

x.description: How far across the frame in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame in fractions of its height.

geometry.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame

tilt.description: How far a group tilts in depth about axes through its anchor point in the slide's plane. It is in degrees.

x.description: It turns about the horizontal axis. It is 0 when left out. With a positive x, its top turns away from the viewer. CSS's `rotateX()` turns the same way. A 3D object's `rotation.x` turns the other way.

y.description: It turns about the vertical axis. It is 0 when left out. With a positive y, its left side comes forward. The y turn comes first, then the x turn.

auto-layout.description: How a group places its members one after another. The defaults are direction vertical, gap 0, align start, and reference-point start. Members are placed in their order in the `objects` list. Hidden members, members with `ignore-auto-layout`, and lines attached to an object are skipped.

direction.description: Whether the members run down or across.

gap.description: The space between one member and the next.

align.description: How the members line up across the layout's direction.

reference-point.description: Which point of the members' box stays at the group's frame as the members grow or shrink: its start, middle, or end along the layout's direction.

anyOf.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

A theme object's file for each color scheme. A dark scheme can then use a file of its own. An image, video, audio, or model object can have a file map in place of a single file. Every file in the map is the same type. A placeholder has one file, not a map.

light.description: The file for the light scheme, and for other light schemes without their own.

dark.description: The file for the dark scheme, and for other dark schemes without their own.

additionalProperties.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

poster.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

position.description: A point in the 3D space in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

motion-blur.description: The camera's motion blur. Only the 3D layer is blurred. It is blurred only in exported movies and the Agent's rendered frames.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open in frames of the movie. At 0, there is no blur. The default is 0.5. It can be animated.

frame-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the shutter's opening. The default is center.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open. The drawings are then averaged. Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples work the same way. The default is 32.

render-effects.description: The camera's render effects: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces, and of the World's light blocked where surfaces meet. In Cinema 4D's Render Settings, they are Global Illumination and Ambient Occlusion. The effects show wherever the 3D layer shows. Only surfaces in view bounce light. A shadow catcher bounces none. An override replaces the whole record.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what is near them. The default is false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other. A shadow catcher then also darkens where an object rests on it. The default is false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface. The default is 400.

drift.description: The camera's drift. Its offset is in canvas units along the slide's 3D axes. After animation, parenting, and constraints place the camera, the offset is added to its position and its point of interest. A parent's rotation and scale don't change it. The drift runs on the slide's own clock. That clock starts when the slide's transition in begins. It runs on through the slide's steps, waits, and transition out. While t is less than `duration`, the added offset at t seconds on that clock is `offset` × (1 − t ÷ `duration`)². The offset decreases to zero at `duration` and stays zero afterward. Stills and the editor show the camera without its drift. A slide has no drift when a scroll transition enters or leaves it.

offset.description: Where the camera starts: an {x, y, z} offset from its set position. An axis left out doesn't move.

duration.description: How many seconds after the slide begins to appear the camera comes to rest.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object. Cinema 4D's Position constraint works the same way. Only the camera can have it. With a spring, the camera follows on a spring with that response and damping ratio. It trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. If the spring is still moving 10 seconds after what it follows has stopped, the camera halts where it got to. It stops short of its target. It stays there until a click moves what it follows again. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as follow. It is unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.follow.strength`.

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows.

target-node.description: The name of a node in the target's model, such as ball. The camera follows the node as the model's Action moves it. Without it, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: A list of the 3D space's axes the camera follows on, such as `["x"]`. Without it, the camera follows on all three.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera follows the target at an offset: its own offset from the slide's center at z 0, added to the target's point. With false, it is at the target's point. The default is true.

strength.description: How far the camera moves to the point it follows: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on. It has the `damping-ratio` and `response` of a keyframe's `spring` interpolation. Without it, the camera follows exactly.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly the spring is damped. At 1, it is critically damped. Less damping swings further.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter response catches up sooner.

anyOf.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

A theme object's file for each color scheme. A dark scheme can then use a file of its own. An image, video, audio, or model object can have a file map in place of a single file. Every file in the map is the same type. A placeholder has one file, not a map.

light.description: The file for the light scheme, and for other light schemes without their own.

dark.description: The file for the dark scheme, and for other dark schemes without their own.

additionalProperties.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

anyOf.description: A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target. Cinema 4D's Aim constraint works the same way. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as look. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.look.strength`.

node.description: The name of the model's node that turns, such as Head. Without it, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light whose origin it turns toward. With `camera`, it turns toward the camera.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target in its GLB's axes. In those axes, y is up, and a model faces along +z. The default is z.

strength.description: How far it turns toward the target: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. It applies to the result of the constraints before it. The default is 1. It can be animated.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as the model scales along its own axes. The volume is measured at the model's scale before animation. Every key except `id` and `type` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as squash. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.squash.strength`.

mode.description: When the volume is kept. With `strict`, it always is. With `uniform`, it is kept while the model scales evenly. With `single-axis`, it is kept while only the free axis scales. The default is strict.

free-axis.description: The axis whose scale is animated. The other two follow to keep the volume. The default is y.

volume.description: The volume to keep. It is a multiple of the model's volume before animation. The default is 1.

strength.description: How strongly it keeps the volume: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

size.description: An area light's size along its own axes in canvas units. In Redshift's Area Light, they are Size X and Size Y.

x.description: Its width, along its own x.

y.description: Its height, along its own y.

position.description: A floor's height in the 3D space. A floor is level and goes on without end. Cinema 4D's Floor works the same way. So a floor's position has only y. Without a position, the floor is at the slide's bottom edge.

y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge in canvas units.

objects.description: The master's objects, back to front. They are behind a layout's and a slide's objects, except one placed by id. The camera and the World are among them. Left out, they have their defaults.

text.description: The words of the master's own text, table, chart, and shape objects by object id.

save-id.description: The id of the save that last wrote the file as an editor handed over the shared presentation, closed it, or signed out. Other tools leave it unchanged.

anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about. A group also tilts about it. It is in fractions of the box the object is drawn at: its frame; a growing text box's box at the size of its words; a table's box at its columns' widths and its rows' heights; or a group's members' box measured at the group's rotation. Without one, an object turns and scales about its center. A text box that grows turns and scales about the point its text grows from. An object's own anchor point needs both x and y. Leaving it out is the only way to the default.

x.description: How far across the box in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the box in fractions of its height.

color.description: a color role or a hex color

crop.description: An image's or a video's zoom and focus inside its frame.

scale.description: How far it is zoomed. At 1, an image fits its frame as its `scale-mode` sets, and a background covers the slide. Above 1, it is zoomed in. Below 1, it is zoomed out.

focal-point.description: The point that stays in view: {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the image, across and down.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. First, what the object paints grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far it reaches in canvas units. It is at most 100 when the slide's shorter side is 1080 or less. The limit grows in proportion on a larger slide. It is 200 at 3840 × 2160.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way.

offset.description: How far it falls: {x, y} across and down in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups. A flip doesn't mirror it. A background's offset is in the slide's axes.

color.description: Its color: a color role, or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece. `based-on` sets whether a piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade-length 1, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 1.

delivery.description: `by-paragraph`: each paragraph enters on the step whose paragraph cue names it. It needs based-on `paragraph` and no seed. Order, spread, pause, and progress must be at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter in seconds. With interpolation hold, each paragraph appears when its cue is reached. A step that has only paragraphs' cues lasts as long as they take.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter: opacity, offset, scale, rotation, and blur.

offset.description: How far it starts from where it rests: {x, y} across and down in ems.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is: its radius in ems. It is never wider than the widest blur the object key `blur` allows on the slide.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

fade-length.description: The fraction of each piece's entrance its fade lasts. The fade starts with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece. It applies only with based-on `character`.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. The wait starts once the pieces before have arrived.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. It is animated by steps.

exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece. Its pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's pieces. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade-length 1, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 0.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting: opacity, offset, scale, rotation, and blur.

offset.description: How far it ends from where it rests: {x, y} across and down in ems.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is: its radius in ems. It is never wider than the widest blur the object key `blur` allows on the slide.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

fade-length.description: The fraction of each piece's exit its fade lasts. The fade ends with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece. It applies only with based-on `character`.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. The wait starts once the pieces before have left.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. It is animated by steps.

flat-scale.description: A flat object's scale along its own axes. The object scales about its `anchor-point`. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

frame.description: An object's position and size in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's, an audio object's, and a group's frame has only x and y: their contents, an icon, or members give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom. A group has a frame only with `auto-layout`. Its frame is the position of its members' box. Its `reference-point` says which point of the box that is: the top left in the group's rotation, or the middle or end along the layout's direction.

x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. For a group, it is the point `reference-point` names.

y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows and it has no `anchor-point`, it turns and scales about a point on its top edge. For a group, it is the point `reference-point` names.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line is in the box the object is drawn at. It turns about its middle by `angle`. By default it crosses the box through its center. It is the same in CSS.

x.description: The x of its middle in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: The y of its middle in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

length.description: Its length in fractions of the box's diagonal.

stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors and their positions.

center.description: The center of a radial gradient: {x, y}.

x.description: Its x in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: Its y in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

shape.description: With `circle`, a radial gradient is round in any box. Without it, the gradient reaches the corners of the box it spans.

stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors and their positions.

line-end.description: A line end attached to an object.

object.description: The id of the object it attaches to on the same slide or composition.

side.description: Which side of the object it attaches to. With `auto`, it attaches to the side that faces the other end.

last-position.description: The point the end is drawn at when the slide has no such object, or when a line can't attach to it: {x, y}. Without a last position, the line isn't drawn then.

mark.description: How italic, highlighted, struck-through, or code text looks. Bold has the same keys except `font-weight`.

font-family.description: The font role the text uses. The theme sets a font family for each role.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

case.description: The letter case the text is shown in. The text itself stays as typed. With `title`, the first letter of each word is a capital.

model-node-name.description: the name of one of the model's nodes

nonblank-line.description: one line that isn't blank and has no control characters

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000"

point-frame.description: An object's position and size in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's, an audio object's, and a group's frame has only x and y: their contents, an icon, or members give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom. A group has a frame only with `auto-layout`. Its frame is the position of its members' box. Its `reference-point` says which point of the box that is: the top left in the group's rotation, or the middle or end along the layout's direction.

x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. For a group, it is the point `reference-point` names.

y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows and it has no `anchor-point`, it turns and scales about a point on its top edge. For a group, it is the point `reference-point` names.

repeater.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. The defaults are 1 for `scale` and `end-opacity`, the center for `anchor-point`, and 0 for the other optional numbers.

copies.description: How many copies there are. The original counts as one.

position.description: The move from each copy to the next: {x, y} across and down. It is measured in the turned and scaled axes of the copy before.

rotation.description: How far each copy is turned clockwise from the one before.

scale.description: How much each copy is scaled from the one before. At 1, each copy is the same size as the one before.

anchor-point.description: The point the copies turn and scale about: {x, y}, both given. Each is a fraction of the box the object is drawn at, across and down.

stagger.description: How much later each copy plays the object's animation than the one before. A copy can play it up to (copies − 1) × `stagger` + `stagger-randomness` later.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity. It is a fraction of the object's opacity. The copies between fade toward it.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random. It is a fraction of its size.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random.

seed.description: The random seed: the same seed gives the same copies.

scheme.description: One color scheme: whether it is light or dark, and its colors. Every theme has light and dark, and it can have more.

appearance.description: Whether the scheme is light or dark. The scheme named light is light, and the one named dark is dark.

background.description: The slide's base color, under everything else.

accent.description: The color for emphasis: a shape's default fill, highlighted text, and a chart's first series or slice.

stroke.description: The color of a table's grid, and of any outline or line set to it.

space-euler.description: A 3D object's rotation about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. It is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode. An object's own rotation in degrees needs x, y, and z.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-position.description: A point in the 3D space in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

space-quaternion.description: A 3D object's rotation about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. It is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode. An object's own rotation in degrees needs x, y, and z.

w.description: A quaternion's w. It is used in quaternion mode only.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-scale.description: A 3D object's scale along its own axes, about its origin. A negative scale mirrors the object along that axis. Objects parented to a light are scaled with it. An area light's surface is scaled too. A move between two scales of one sign stops at 0. A wave can take a scale past 0.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color is along the gradient from 0 to 1. A stop is never before the previous one.

theme-file-path.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

time-trim.description: The part of a video or audio file, or of a clip's Action, that plays.

start.description: Where it starts in seconds into the file or the Action. The default is 0.

end.description: Where it ends in seconds into the file or the Action. It must come after start. Without it, the file or the Action plays to its end.

trim.description: The drawn part of a path's or a line's stroke.

start.description: Where the drawn part starts along the stroke.

end.description: Where the drawn part ends along the stroke.

wipe.description: A reveal behind a moving straight edge.

progress.description: How much of the object shows. At 0, none of it shows. At 1, all of it shows.

angle.description: Which way the edge travels in degrees clockwise from up. The angle turns with the object.

feather.description: How wide the soft edge is. Across it, the object fades from shown to hidden.
